title: Single-cluster pull-down assay for visualization and characterization of nanoclusters and condensates
author: Paul, Myong

steps.title: Obtain and purify target protein
steps.instruction: Purify the protein of interest using workflows appropriate for the system (e.g., recombinant expression and purification). For FUS, purify both untagged and MBP‑tagged constructs; for other cluster‑forming proteins, use suitable strategies.

steps.title: Prepare tagged and untagged fractions
steps.instruction: Generate a majority untagged protein population to preserve native clustering, a small fraction of tagged protein for surface capture, and a fluorescently labeled fraction derived from the untagged construct. Typical concentrations are ~30–50 nM tagged protein and ~5–10 nM labeled untagged protein, while unlabeled untagged protein is varied.

steps.title: Fluorescently label untagged protein
steps.instruction: Label purified untagged protein using an appropriate dye‑conjugation strategy (maleimide or NHS chemistry). Perform fluorophore labeling (e.g., Cy3 or Cy5 NHS ester) following standard protocols, quantify labeling efficiency and keep labeling ≤10 % of the protein population, remove excess free dye, and verify that labeling does not significantly perturb clustering behavior.

steps.title: Perform protein quality control
steps.instruction: Confirm protein purity >90 % by SDS‑PAGE and clarify protein stocks by high‑speed centrifugation (15,000–20,000 × g for 10–15 min at 4 °C) prior to cluster assembly.

steps.title: Aliquot and store protein stocks
steps.instruction: Aliquot purified protein to avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles, store under conditions that minimize spontaneous aggregation, thaw samples on ice and use immediately.

steps.title: Clean and activate glass surfaces
steps.instruction: Place 3" × 1" glass slides (~1 mm thick) and 24 × 40 mm coverslips in a glass staining jar. If reusing, soak in ethanol or acetone for several hours, rinse thoroughly, then sonicate in 5 % (w/v) laboratory detergent for 5–10 min at 20–25 °C. Rinse extensively with running water followed by Milli‑Q water. Treat with 1 M KOH and sonicate for 30–45 min, rinse repeatedly with Milli‑Q water until neutralized, dry under nitrogen, and flame‑dry each surface for 1–2 s with a propane torch. Allow to cool.

steps.title: Amino‑silanize slides and coverslips
steps.instruction: Prepare a silanization solution of 95 % methanol, 5 % acetic acid, and ~1–2 % aminosilane (v/v). Fully immerse slides and coverslips, incubate in the dark for ~30–40 min without agitation, rinse thoroughly with methanol then Milli‑Q water, and dry completely under nitrogen.

steps.title: Couple PEG and biotin‑PEG to surface
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 100 mM sodium bicarbonate buffer (pH ~8.3) by dissolving 84 mg NaHCO₃ in 10 mL Milli‑Q water. Dissolve mPEG‑SVA together with biotin‑PEG‑SVA (1–2 % molar ratio; typically 1–2 mg biotin‑PEG‑SVA and the remainder mPEG‑SVA to total ~100 mg PEG) in the buffer, mix gently, and centrifuge 5,000–10,000 × g for 1–2 min at 20–25 °C to remove particulates. Immediately apply ~60–80 µL of this PEG solution to each slide, overlay with a coverslip to form a thin film, and incubate in a humidified dark chamber for 3–5 h at 20–25 °C. (Optional: repeat PEGylation after washing and drying for extremely low background.)

steps.title: Wash and store PEG‑passivated slides
steps.instruction: After PEG incubation, carefully separate slide and coverslip with forceps, rinse thoroughly with Milli‑Q water, dry under nitrogen, and store dried PEG‑passivated slides in sealed containers at –20 °C. Mark the non‑functionalized side (e.g., with a diamond pen) for later identification.

steps.title: Assemble PEG‑passivated flow chamber
steps.instruction: Cut two parallel strips of double‑sided tape (~1 mm wide) and place them lengthwise on a PEG‑passivated slide to define the channel, aligning the tape with pre‑drilled inlet and outlet holes. Place the PEG‑passivated coverslip (functionalized side inward) on top of the tape, apply gentle pressure along the edges (e.g., with a pipette tip), seal exposed edges with rapid‑curing epoxy and cure for 5–10 min, attach inlet reservoirs and outlet tubing using trimmed pipette tips and epoxy if needed, then slowly fill the channel with buffer to verify no leakage or trapped air bubbles. The chamber is now ready for surface functionalization.

steps.title: Prepare nanocluster mixture
steps.instruction: In experimental buffer, combine MBP‑FUS (~30–50 nM), fluorophore‑labeled FUS (~5–10 nM), and a variable concentration of unlabeled FUS (~50–500 nM). Mix gently; the mixture will assemble into nanoclusters within the flow chamber over time. Keep the tagged protein concentration low to minimize perturbation while ensuring efficient surface capture.

steps.title: Load mixture and initiate assembly
steps.instruction: Immediately load the nanocluster mixture into the reservoir of the assembled flow chamber; assembly proceeds in situ.

steps.title: Acquire real‑time assembly kinetics
steps.instruction: Pre‑mix tagged protein (~30–50 nM) and fluorescently labeled untagged protein (~5–10 nM) in experimental buffer at 20–25 °C. Initiate assembly by adding unlabeled protein at the desired concentration (e.g., 200–1000 nM) and mix gently. Load ~100 µL of the mixture into the reservoir, begin controlled flow (~0.1 mL/min) using a syringe pump while recording continuously. Record movies at a defined time resolution (e.g., 100 ms/frame) for an appropriate duration (e.g., 5–10 min for FUS). Maintain constant laser power, camera settings, and ambient temperature (20–25 °C) throughout acquisition.

steps.title: Perform FRAP on surface clusters
steps.instruction: Immobilize Cy5‑labeled nanoclusters on the surface as described, fix the imaging region and avoid stage movement. Photobleach a selected region using near‑maximal laser intensity for ~1–2 min to achieve substantial fluorescence reduction. Record fluorescence recovery at defined intervals (e.g., every 5–10 s over 5–180 s) under low laser power to minimize additional bleaching. Extract single‑cluster intensity traces and fit recovery curves to single‑ or double‑exponential models to obtain characteristic recovery times. Keep laser power, exposure time, and camera gain constant across experiments; avoid detector saturation. Cy5 is recommended for FRAP due to efficient photobleaching.

steps.title: Process movies and analyze data
steps.instruction: Process raw movies using a calibrated channel‑mapping file generated during instrument calibration. Extract single‑cluster fluorescence time traces with IDL‑based scripts, then analyze in MATLAB. Visualize images and inspect spots with ImageJ or equivalent. Determine cluster size by segmenting projected cluster area and converting to physical units using calibrated pixel size. Quantify assembly kinetics by measuring changes in cluster area (or fluorescence intensity) over time. Analyze molecular exchange by fitting intensity traces to exponential models to obtain exchange times. Perform statistical comparisons using appropriate tests; for pairwise comparisons use an unpaired two‑tailed Student’s t‑test when normality assumptions are met. Include multiple independent slide preparations and biological replicates for reproducibility.
